extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and requirements for withdrawing or dismissing appeals to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, reopening prosecution, and seeking judicial review (appeals/civil actions) from Board decisions. Covers filing, timing, fees, service, examiner actions, and consequences (e.g., abandonment, cancellation of claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of Appeal (general effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appeal is withdrawn after the period for reply to the final rejection has expired, the application is considered abandoned as of the date the appeal was withdrawn unless there are allowed claims in the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A letter abandoning the application filed under 37 CFR 1.138 is effective as of the date of recognition by the Office (or another date if specified). If a brief was filed timely and appellant withdraws prior to transfer of jurisdiction to the Board under 37 CFR 41.35(a), the application is returned to the examiner; if after transfer, dismissal is handled by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Continued Examination (RCE) treated as withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 while an appeal is pending is treated as a withdrawal of the appeal by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reopen prosecution via RCE, the RCE must include a submission responsive within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.111 to the last outstanding Office action and the RCE fee under 37 CFR 1.17(e). RCE practice under 1.114 does not apply to utility/plant applications filed before June 8, 1995, design applications, or reexamination proceedings (see 1.114(d) and MPEP § 706.07(h)). An RCE filed without the appropriate fee or submission in an application with no allowed claims will result in abandonment; to avoid abandonment file the RCE in compliance with 37 CFR 1.114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations permitting reopening prosecution while appeal pending
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may request prosecution be reopened in response to (A) a new ground of rejection in an examiner's answer or (B) a substitute examiner's answer written in response to a Board remand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In both situations appellant may file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 that addresses the new ground/rejection within two months from the mailing of the examiner's (or substitute) answer (see MPEP §§ 1207.03 and 1207.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify Board when refiling/filing RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should promptly inform the Clerk of the Board in writing when they decide to refile or abandon an application containing an appeal awaiting decision, and advise the Board when an RCE is filed in such an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to exercise diligence may result in the Board refusing an otherwise proper request to vacate its decision. Prompt notice avoids rendering decisions in applications already refiled as continuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner handling when appeal withdrawn and no allowed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon withdrawal of an appeal, an application having no allowed claims is abandoned; examiner actions depend on claim status (cancel, hold abandoned, or issue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: (A) If claim 1 allowed, cancel rejected dependent claims and issue with claim 1 only. (B) If all claims rejected, hold application abandoned. (C) If only dependent claims are allowable except for dependency and no time remains to redraft, hold abandoned. (D) If independent claim allowed, cancel dependent rejected claims and issue on the allowed claim. In ex parte reexamination, issue a certificate under 37 CFR 1.570.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Standing Allowed when appeal withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application contains allowed claims as well as claims on appeal, withdrawal of the appeal does not operate as an abandonment of the application; it is a withdrawal of the appeal as to those claims and authority returns to the examiner to cancel the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment canceling the appealed claims is equivalent to a withdrawal of the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial Withdrawal — removing claims from appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: To remove claims from consideration on appeal, the appellant must submit an amendment canceling those claims (see 37 CFR 41.31(c) and 41.33).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appellant may choose not to present arguments or rely on particular evidence for certain claim rejections; however, such arguments and evidence are waived for purposes of the appeal and the Board may summarily sustain any grounds of rejection not argued (see MPEP §§ 1205.02 and 1214.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sua sponte dismissal for failure to respond to new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to respond to a new ground of rejection in an examiner's answer (or to a substitute examiner's answer after remand) by filing a reply brief or a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 within two months, the appeal will be sua sponte dismissed by the Board as to the claims subject to the new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 12.279.02 may be used to dismiss claims subject to new ground(s) if no timely reply is filed. The substitute examiner's answer may also include new grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal because no brief was filed (timing and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: If no brief is filed within the time prescribed by 37 CFR 41.37, the appeal stands dismissed by operation of the rule (but do not dismiss until the extension period under 37 CFR 1.136(a) has expired).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications with no allowed claims will be abandoned. Claims allowable except for dependency are treated as rejected. If an amendment obviously places the application in condition for allowance the primary examiner may recommend entering it (see MPEP § 1214.07) subject to supervisory concurrence. If formal matters remain, examiner may correct by examiner's amendment or use form paragraph 12.209 to set a shortened period for reply; further prosecution is closed except as to formal matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 12.209 — Appeal Dismissed with Allowed Claims and Formal Matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph to notify applicant that appeal stands dismissed for failure to file a brief but application will be passed to issue on allowed claim(s) provided specified formal matters are corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must correct formal matters within a shortened statutory period (TWO MONTHS) to avoid abandonment; extensions under 1.136 may be available but cannot carry beyond the six-month statutory maximum (35 U.S.C. 133). Notes specify use only if notice of appeal filed on/after Jan 23, 2012, and only if formal matters cannot be handled by examiner’s amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal because brief was held non-compliant
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal will be dismissed if an applicant fails to timely and fully reply to a notice of noncompliance under 37 CFR 41.37(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no allowed claims remain, application is abandoned as of the date the reply to the notice was due. Applicant may petition to revive and to reinstate the appeal, but must file a proper reply to the notice of noncompliance before a petition is considered; reinstatement requires a showing equivalent to a petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for failure to pay appeal forwarding fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appeal forwarding fee required under 37 CFR 41.20(b)(4) is not paid within the period set in 37 CFR 41.45(a), the appeal will stand dismissed (see 37 CFR 41.45(b) and MPEP § 1208.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences mirror other dismissals: no allowed claims -> abandonment; allowable-except-dependency treated as rejected. Examiner examples (A-D) guide cancellation/issuance/holding abandoned. Formal matters handled by examiner's amendment or form paragraph 12.209; further prosecution closed except for formal matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal following substitute examiner's answer after remand
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to timely respond to a substitute examiner's answer mailed in response to a Board remand (37 CFR 41.50(a)), appellant must within two months either (1) reopen prosecution by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or (2) maintain appeal by filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41; failure leads to sua sponte dismissal as to the claims subject to the remanded rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 12.286 may be used. If some claims are not subject to the remanded rejection, the appeal continues as to those claims and the application will be forwarded to the Board after mailing of the communication. Examiner notes for bracketed insertions provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal following remand from the Board (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal may be dismissed if appellant fails to timely and fully reply to a substitute examiner's answer written in response to a Board remand for reconsideration of a rejection under 37 CFR 41.50(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant must within two months either file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41; failure results in dismissal as to claims subject to the remanded rejection and cancellation of those claims. Examiner may use form paragraph 12.286 to inform appellant of options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for appeals to the Federal Circuit (35 U.S.C. 141 / 37 CFR 90.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: To appeal a Board decision to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, the appellant must (A) file in the USPTO a written notice of appeal directed to the Director (35 U.S.C. 142), (B) file a copy with the Board per 37 CFR 41.10/42.6, and (C) file with the Clerk of the Federal Circuit a copy of the notice and pay the docket fee (Federal Circuit Rule 52).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an appeal to the Federal Circuit waives the right to proceed under 35 U.S.C. 145. Parties in ex parte reexamination, IPR, post-grant review, covered business method review, or derivation proceedings have additional service/notice obligations (e.g., 37 CFR 1.550(f), 42.6(e)) and must include sufficient information to allow the Director to decide whether to intervene under 35 U.S.C. 143.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service rules for appeals, elections, and civil actions (37 CFR 90.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies where and how notices and copies must be filed and served for appeals (35 U.S.C. 141), elections under 141(d), and civil actions under 146.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of appeal must be filed with the Director as provided in § 104.2 and a copy with the PTAB as provided in § 41.10(a)/(b) or § 42.6(b). Notices in certain proceedings must contain information to permit the Director to determine intervention rights and must be served per applicable rules. For civil actions under 146, a copy of the complaint must be filed with the PTAB and Office of the Solicitor within five business days after filing in district court; failure may result in further USPTO action. Service copies of court papers where Director is a party must be served on the Office of the Solicitor (Rule 5(b) & Appellate Rule 25(b) guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing notice of appeal or commencing civil action (37 CFR 90.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines: generally the notice of appeal or civil action must be filed/commenced within sixty-three (63) days after the date of the final Board decision (subject to other statutory provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearing, if timely requested, resets the 63‑day period to run from action on the rehearing. If deadline falls on a federal holiday in D.C., time is extended to next non-holiday weekday. Director may extend time for filing or commencing civil action for good cause if requested before expiration, or for excusable neglect if requested after expiration; requests per § 104.2. Time computations and additional requirements (paying fees, complying with FRAP and Federal Circuit rules) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for extensions to seek judicial review (37 CFR 90.3(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may extend the time to file an appeal or commence a civil action for (A) good cause if requested before expiration; or (B) excusable neglect if requested after expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard mirrors federal court standards. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(b), 1.550(c), and fee extensions under 1.136(a) are not available to extend the time for seeking judicial review once a decision or decision on rehearing has been entered. Requests should be filed as provided in § 104.2; a copy may be provided to the Office of the Solicitor (Mail Stop 8) to expedite handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative file and amendments during judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrative file of an application under judicial review will not be opened to the public by the USPTO unless otherwise available; during judicial review the application or reexamination is not under examiner or Board jurisdiction unless remanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments can be admitted only under 37 CFR 1.198. The 'last' decision (decision or decision on rehearing) determines when extension standards apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of court papers on the Director / Office of the Solicitor
rubrics_metrics.description: All service copies of court papers filed in court proceedings in which the Director is a party must be served on the Office of the Solicitor, either by hand (8:30 A.M.–5:00 P.M. EST) to the specified address or by mail to the specified P.O. Box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide correct mail service address (Mail Stop 8, Office of the Solicitor, USPTO). The mail service address must not be supplemented to refer to the Director or USPTO, and must not be used for non-court papers; any non-court papers mailed there will be returned. Rule 5(b) (civil procedure) and Appellate Rule 25(b) (appellate procedure) guidance on serving counsel applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory overview of appeal routes and consequences (35 U.S.C. §§ 141, 142, 143, 144, 145, 146, 306)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarizes statutory rights: appeals to the Federal Circuit (35 U.S.C. 141), notice of appeal (142), Director's transmission of certified record and right to intervene (143), court decision and mandate (144), civil action to obtain patent (145), appeals in derivation proceedings and elections under 146, and reexamination appeal rules (306).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an appeal to the Federal Circuit waives the right to proceed under 35 U.S.C. 145. For derivation proceedings, an adverse party can elect to proceed under 146 which affects remedies and timeframes. For reexamination, patent owner appeals and judicial review are governed by the cited statutes. The court may adjudge entitlement to a patent and require applicant payment of court proceeding expenses.
